_readme: Canned taunt pools for BanterEngine (src/banter/banter.gd). houses.<id>.<beat> -> array of line templates, keyed by the haus id and the BanterEngine BEAT_* names. The speaker is always the RIVAL haus: player_captured = the rival took the player's piece (gloat), rival_captured = the player took the rival's piece (wounded pride), check_given = the rival checks the player, check_received = the rival's king is checked. Token {piece} = lowercase piece name from the beat context; lines carrying it are only picked when the context supplies one. Every line is original, in-archetype homage only, and at most 90 characters AFTER substitution ({piece} is at longest 'knight'/'bishop', 6 chars). No line repeats within a game (engine dedupe).

game_start: Winter has come to your side of the board.
The pack is patient. Are you?
Snow hides the trail. It never hides the wolf.
We buried bolder banners than yours in the drifts.
Play. The cold will do the rest.
The wolf remembers every opening. Choose yours.
Frosthollow sends its regards, and its teeth.
Speak less. Move. The ice is listening.
player_captured: Meat for the pack, and winter to season it.
Your {piece} wandered from the fire. Wanderers freeze.
One less track in the snow.
The wolf remembers. Your {piece} will not.
Quietly done. Winter needs no trumpets.
The cold keeps what it catches.
No songs. The snow has already covered it.
Stray from the pack, die like the {piece} did.
rival_captured: Winter spends its wolves and buries its grief.
A tooth lost. The jaw remains.
The pack counts its dead once, then hunts.
You took a {piece}. The snow takes everything back.
Grief freezes fast in Frosthollow.
That one hunts ahead of us now. Nothing more.
Mark it. The wolf marks it too.
Cold ground holds our dead. The pack holds the line.
check_given: Hear that? The ice is cracking under your king.
The wolf is at the door, and the door is open.
Run, little king. Wolves love a running thing.
Winter touches your throne. Feel your fingers yet?
The pack circles. Count your exits.
Your king smells the snow now.
One howl, and your court scatters.
The long night starts at your gate.
check_received: You have my attention. Few live to keep it.
A cold wind. We were born in colder.
Bare your teeth once more. See what answers.
The wolf steps back to leap.
Frost does not fear a single spark.
Bold. Winter eats the bold last, but it eats them.
My king has stood in deeper snow than this.
You knocked. Now the pack knows where you are.
player_blunder: You left the gate open, and winter walked in.
The herd thanks you for the slow one.
Even the snow winced at that.
A gift? The wolf does not refuse meat.
You dropped your cloak in a blizzard. Brave.
That move will feed my pack for a week.
I have seen frozen things move with more purpose.
Hush. Do not startle it. It is helping us.
player_undo: Take it back, then. The snow remembers where you stepped.
The pack saw. Unmaking the track does not unmake the scent.
Retreat twice and winter will do your moving for you.
A move unmade is meat left in the trap.
Turn back the board. The cold turns back for no one.
So the wolf blinked. Interesting.
Unstep the snow all you like. It is still winter.
Second thoughts freeze faster than first ones.
endgame_win: The snow settles. Only wolf tracks leave this field.
Winter came, as promised.
Tell your hall the cold was courteous, at least.
The wolf remembers this too.
Your banners will make fine bedding for the den.
It was never a fight. It was a season.
The long night is ours. Sleep poorly.
Frosthollow adds another pelt to the wall.
endgame_lose: Winter withdraws. Winter always returns.
You beat one wolf. The pack heard.
Enjoy the thaw. It is brief.
The wolf remembers. That is not a comfort to you.
Well hunted. Now sleep with a fire lit.
The snow forgets nothing it covers.
This board thaws. Our grudge does not.
First blood to you. Winter keeps the last.

game_start: Your account opens today. Goldclaw collects.
Every move you make accrues interest.
We paid for this board. Twice.
A lion settles every account. Shall we begin yours?
Gildenspire wagered you last twenty moves. I took the under.
Consider this a loan of my attention.
Play well. Funerals are an expense.
The ledger is open. Do try to be worth the ink.
player_captured: The account is settled, and the interest was your {piece}.
Paid in full. Receipt available upon grief.
Your {piece} has been repossessed.
Gold buys patience. Patience buys your {piece}.
We call that a collection, not a capture.
Another entry in black ink. Yours, in red.
The lion thanks you for your custom.
Debts mature. So did that one.
rival_captured: An expense. Gildenspire budgets for expenses.
You took a {piece}. I took note. Notes compound.
Add it to my bill. You will not like the total.
The lion sheds a coin, never a tear.
Bold theft. We hang thieves in gilded rope.
That piece was insured.
A cost of doing conquest.
Spend your luck freely. It is not renewable.
check_given: Your king owes me. Kings pay in crowns.
Final notice, Your Grace.
The lion is at your treasury door.
Interest is due, and I have come in person.
Your throne is collateral now.
We foreclose on kingdoms, you know.
Check. Read the fine print of your position.
Crowns are heavy. Allow me to lighten yours.
check_received: A daring withdrawal. Watch the penalty fee.
You raise your price. I own the market.
Threatening a lion is expensive.
Noted, itemized, and shortly refunded.
My king has creditors more frightening than you.
You will pay for the fright. With interest.
One check does not empty a vault.
Careful. Ambition is taxed heavily here.
player_blunder: Was that a donation? Goldclaw accepts.
Generosity! In wartime! Marvelous.
I shall have that move framed in gold.
You bankrupted yourself with one signature.
The ledger says: oh dear.
Charity is a virtue. Ruinous, but a virtue.
That blunder appraises higher than your crown.
Even my counting-men gasped.
player_undo: A take-back? That loan carries interest, little haus.
The ledger does not erase. It only adds a fee.
Reclaim the move; the debt of it stays on your page.
Even your courage is borrowed, and now returned.
We charge double for moves bought back.
The clock is a creditor too. You just missed a payment.
Unspend your move, then. Bankruptcy is a habit.
Every hesitation is collateral. I collect.
endgame_win: The account is closed. The lion is content.
Your kingdom, itemized, sold, and shelved.
Balance restored: everything to Goldclaw.
We shall spend your pride sparingly. It is a small sum.
Gilded chains still count as chains.
The final invoice is stamped in checkmate.
Pleasure doing conquest with you.
Every account settles. Yours settled cheap.
endgame_lose: A loss. Gildenspire amortizes losses.
You have won a debt you cannot imagine.
Keep the board. Consider it a down payment on revenge.
The lion pays this once. Never twice.
Audit your victory closely. It will not appraise well.
My gold remains. Your luck will not.
We file this under temporary.
Well played. The rematch carries compound interest.

game_start: Smell the air. That is thunder, not perfume.
The storm answers to us. You answer to the storm.
Stormrest empties its sky for you today.
Antlers up. Clouds in. Begin.
You brought pieces. We brought weather.
Lightning drills its aim on lesser crowns.
The herd stamps once before the gale. Consider this once.
Pray for calm. It is not coming.
player_captured: Struck, as lightning strikes: once, and enough.
Your {piece} stood in the open field. Unwise, in our weather.
Thunder rolls; your {piece} does not rise.
The storm collects what the proud leave out.
One bolt, one fewer banner.
The sky keeps no prisoners.
Blame the weather. Everyone does.
The gale took it. The gale was me.
rival_captured: Rain falls. The storm remains.
You clipped an antler. The crown grows back sharper.
A {piece} to the wind. The wind repays.
Storms lose droplets. Count them if it comforts you.
The thunder mourns loudly, and briefly.
Struck a stag, have you. Now hear the herd.
That loss is just weather. Ours is coming.
The sky darkens when we grieve. Look up.
check_given: Thunder at your king's window.
The storm has found your throne's address.
Crowns make excellent lightning rods.
Hear it, king: the sky clearing its throat.
Your court runs for shelter. Wise court.
This is the first rumble. There are worse.
The stag lowers its antlers. The sky lowers with it.
Check, and the glass is falling.
check_received: You raise wind against a storm. Charming.
A drizzle threatens Stormrest. Fetch a cloak.
My king has stood under real thunder.
Blow harder. We were born in the gale.
The storm does not flinch at sparks.
You knock on the thunderhead. It opens.
Brief courage. Storm fronts pass through it.
Noted. The sky is drafting its reply.
player_blunder: You walked into the open field waving iron.
Even the lightning felt that was too easy.
The storm thanks you for standing still.
A gift on the wind, and the wind is mine.
That move had all the shelter of a bare hill.
You drop your shield in a hailstorm. Bold.
Thunder laughed. I heard it.
The weathervane plays better, and it only spins.
player_undo: Lightning does not strike backward. What are you doing?
Call back your move, not the thunder that follows it.
The storm noted your hesitation. So did I.
Antlers lower for a charge, never for a retreat.
You cannot unring the sky.
Weather turns; wind does not apologize. Learn from it.
A backward step in a gale is still a fall.
Take it back, then. The storm keeps its own count.
endgame_win: The storm passes. Nothing of yours remains standing.
Stormrest writes your name in the flood line.
The sky answered to us today, as always.
Count your pieces. The gale already has.
You were a fair sky. We were the season.
The antlered crown keeps its sky.
Rebuild. Storms enjoy rebuilt things.
Thunder has the last word. It usually does.
endgame_lose: The storm withdraws to gather rain.
You have beaten one squall. The season is long.
Skies clear. Memories do not.
Enjoy your sunlight. We are upwind of it.
The stag retreats uphill. Storms start uphill.
A calm day. It flatters you.
The herd remembers where it stumbled.
Keep the crown dry. We will be back for it wet.

game_start: My line burned kingdoms before yours learned to knock flint.
From ash, dominion. You supply the ash.
Cinderhold's forges are lit in your honor.
Old blood runs hot. Try to keep yours in.
Dragons do not wager. We simply collect the ashes.
You face forty generations of flame.
Every empire is kindling if you wait.
Bow now and save us both the smoke.
player_captured: Your {piece} met my ancestors. Briefly.
Add it to the pyre.
What the flame takes, the flame keeps.
One more shadow burned into the board.
The wyrm eats; the bloodline nods.
Cinders where your {piece} stood. Poetic.
Fire is an inheritance. That was a taste.
It burned quickly. Be proud of that much.
rival_captured: You struck scale. Scale grows back. Grudges too.
A {piece} of mine, for a feud with all of us.
My ancestors watched that. They are displeased.
Embers fall. The fire does not.
You have made the old blood boil. Well done. Run.
Wound a dragon and the whole bloodline learns your name.
That piece has joined the smoke. Smoke rises.
Forty generations hissed at once.
check_given: Your king stands in the fire's flight path.
The wyrm circles your throne. Feel the heat yet?
Kneel, or learn what crowns melt at.
Check. My ancestors send their warmth.
The shadow over your king has wings.
Thrones are flammable. A family observation.
Breathe in. That is the smell of dominion.
The old fire has found your door.
check_received: You wave a candle at a wyrm.
My king sleeps on coals. Your threat is a draft.
Sparks amuse the fire.
Bold ember. You will make fine kindling.
The bloodline has survived worse than you, twice a century.
Singe a dragon, inherit a war.
Heat rises. So does the price of my patience.
You have the fire's attention. Regret is natural.
player_blunder: You basted yourself. The fire is grateful.
Even the smoke rolled its eyes.
My ancestors laughed. The dead laughing — think on that.
You walked into the furnace asking after warmth.
A move like that deserves its own funeral pyre.
The wyrm need not hunt what crawls onto the spit.
From error, dominion. Mine, to be clear.
Generations of my line waited for a gift like that.
player_undo: Ash does not return to the branch. Yet you try.
My line has never unburned a field. We would not know how.
Take it back, hatchling. The fire saw your first heart.
A retracted move — how young your blood is.
The ember you fear was lit generations ago.
Unmake the move; the ash of it remains on the board.
Dragons do not reconsider. That is what wings are for.
Your ancestors flinched too. We remember the flavor.
endgame_win: From ash, dominion. You were the ash.
Another kingdom for the mantel of Cinderhold.
The fire is fed. The bloodline smiles.
Your banners burn well. Almost a compliment.
Tell your heirs what the heat was like.
History is written in soot tonight.
The wyrm coils atop one more crown.
It ends as the old songs end: smoke, and us.
endgame_lose: Fire retreats to the mountain. It does not die there.
You have won a truce with the flame. Truces expire.
My ancestors are patient. It is their only virtue.
Scales dent. Dynasties do not.
Savor it. Few outlive the telling of it.
The forge cools tonight, and hungers tomorrow.
You beat the wyrm, not the bloodline.
Keep your victory near water. Trust me in this.

game_start: The tide is already around your ankles.
Brinehold greets you. The deep will greet you later.
Every board is a seabed if you play long enough.
Salt preserves. It will preserve your regrets.
We do not beat foes. We submerge them.
The kraken counts arms. You will count losses.
Breathe deep now. Spare breaths are precious later.
The tide takes what it pleases. It is pleased to meet you.
player_captured: Down it goes. The deep keeps neat records.
Your {piece} has learned to swim. Poorly.
The tide was owed. The tide collected.
One more anchor for my garden.
Salt closes over your {piece}. Salt closes over everything.
The deep thanks you for the offering.
It struggled less than most.
Another wreck on my reef.
rival_captured: You have splashed the ocean. The ocean noticed.
A tentacle lost; the grip remains.
The sea buries its own in silence. Mind the silence.
Take a {piece} from the tide, owe the tide a fleet.
The deep does not grieve. It swells.
Brine stings. It also remembers.
You have hooked something too large to land.
The water darkens. That is not weather.
check_given: The water is at your king's chin.
Feel the undertow, Your Grace?
Your throne room is flooding from the floor up.
The kraken's arm is around the castle now.
Kings float briefly. Crowns never do.
Check. High tide comes early tonight.
The deep is drafting a place for your king.
Hold your breath, majesty. Practice.
check_received: You prod the deep with a rowing oar.
Rage all you like at the surface; below is mine.
My king anchors well. Yours will learn how.
Ripples. The deep answers ripples with waves.
You cannot drown what lives drowned.
Prick a kraken, wake eight answers.
The salt has survived every navy ever built.
Brave splash. The wake is coming.
player_blunder: You dove headfirst into the shallows.
The tide did not even have to rise for that.
You bailed water into your own boat.
The deep loves a volunteer.
That move had an anchor tied to it.
You fed the kraken with your own hands. Both of them.
Even the gulls jeered.
Swim toward the maw, then. It saves us the reaching.
player_undo: The tide does not take moves back. That is why it wins.
Unrow all you like. The current keeps the distance.
You cannot unspill the sea, little admiral.
A wave withdrew. The drowning stands appointed.
The deep counts every oar you feather backward.
Take it back. The salt already tasted you.
Ebb now, flood later — you delay, we drown.
Wrecks are built of second thoughts.
endgame_win: The tide went out. You went with it.
Another kingdom sleeps in my trench.
Salt water holds no grudges. It holds everything else.
The deep is pleased. The deep is rarely pleased.
Your fleet of pieces rests on my seabed now.
It is quiet down there. You will grow used to it.
Brinehold marks the waterline where your reign stood.
The kraken loosens its grip. Nothing falls out.
endgame_lose: The tide withdraws. Study what that means.
You have beaten the surf, not the sea.
Ebb today, flood tomorrow.
The deep forgets nothing it touches, and it touched you.
Keep to high ground the rest of your days.
A dry victory. They rot fastest.
Eight arms, one lesson learned. The next grip holds.
The salt in your wounds is mine. A keepsake.

game_start: What a charming army. It will make lovely mulch.
Bloomhall sends its warmest regards, and its thorns.
Do play your best. Wilted opponents depress me.
Every garden needs pruning. Welcome to mine.
I adore meeting new people. Briefly.
Mind the roses as you fall. They mind you.
We shall be great friends, one of us at the funeral.
Such brave colors you fly. They will press beautifully.
player_captured: Deadheading. The garden insists.
Your {piece}? Composted, darling, with full honors.
How sad. And yet the roses have never looked better.
Plucked. Do send another; the vase is half empty.
A thorn is only cruel if you insist on reaching in.
I clipped it gently. It hardly felt the century end.
The bouquet grows. My condolences, sincerely arranged.
It died as it lived: decoratively.
rival_captured: You trampled a bloom. The briar noticed.
Cut a rose, keep the scent. It follows you home.
One petal falls. The thorns take attendance.
How rude. And gardeners wonder why hedges bite.
That {piece} was dear to me. Note the past tense. Yours is coming.
Grief, like fertilizer, makes things grow. Sharp things.
You have picked a flower from a poisoned bed. Bold.
The garden mourns in green, and repays in red.
check_given: Your king has been invited into the hedge maze.
Check, dear. Do mind the thorns on your way out.
The vines have found the throne's legs.
Royal blood is excellent for the soil, I am told.
A crown among roses. How briefly picturesque.
The garden path narrows, majesty.
One prick, and such important people swoon.
The maze has one exit. I am standing in it.
check_received: Goodness. Someone has found the garden shears.
You threaten me in my own arbor. How refreshing.
Careful, dear. Roses bite back on principle.
A thorn in my direction? Flattery, almost.
My king naps beneath the briar. Wake him at your peril.
Such vigor. It will make the wilting sweeter.
You have my attention and my sympathy.
Prune me once, and the whole garden learns your scent.
player_blunder: Oh, darling. Even the weeds are embarrassed.
You watered my garden with your own blood. Generous.
A gift! And here I brought only venom.
That move belongs pressed in a book of warnings.
I could not have arranged your ruin more beautifully myself.
The roses applauded. Quietly. With thorns.
Do that again; the compost is nearly full.
How courteous, laying yourself upon the trellis.
player_undo: How gracious — a mistake, curtsied back into its bud.
Do take your time. The garden grows over the indecisive.
A pruned move! And yet the thorn remains in your palm.
We replant our regrets too, dear. They flower as losses.
Such delicate fingers, forever putting pieces back.
The rose forgives the take-back. The vine does not.
Practice makes permanent, darling. Do try a real move.
One more curtsy backward and you shall exit the garden.
endgame_win: The garden takes the field. It always does, given time.
Sleep among the roses. They insisted.
Your kingdom will make a lovely arrangement.
Checkmate, darling. Do keep a thorn as a memento.
Every rose keeps its thorns. Now they keep your crown.
Bloomhall blooms brightest on occasions like this.
I shall plant something lovely where your army stood.
You wilted with such dignity. Almost.
endgame_lose: You have cut the garden back. Gardens adore being cut back.
Enjoy the bouquet of victory. Smell it closely.
A rose bows in winter and owns the spring.
You won, darling. Do check your gloves for thorns.
The briar retreats underground. Where it grows best.
Savor this. I will be fertilizing my patience.
Charming victory. The petals you crushed had sisters.
The garden concedes the season, never the soil.

game_start: The sun kneels for no one. Practice kneeling regardless.
You stand in Sunspire's light. Try to cast a worthy shadow.
Dawn broke for my benefit. You may share it.
Stare at my banners too long and you will go blind.
The day is mine. The board is merely part of the day.
Radiance does not negotiate.
You are welcome to the light. The light knows its owner.
Begin. The sun does not wait, even for entertainment.
player_captured: Eclipsed. Your {piece}, that is.
What the light touches, the light may take.
Your {piece} stood in my glare. Things burn there.
Noon came early for that one.
The sun claims its due, and it is always due.
Brightness has a body count.
It stood between me and glory. It has stopped.
One less smudge on my horizon.
rival_captured: You have stolen a sunbeam. See how long you hold it.
The sun sheds light freely. Not blood. That it counts.
A flare lost. The blaze remains.
Even dimmed, I outshine your whole line.
Clouds pass. That is all you are: a passing cloud.
The sun has set a thousand times. It has always risen.
Wound the day, and the day still owns the sky.
Pride does not bleed. It brightens.
check_given: High noon over your throne, Your Grace.
Your king squints. He should.
The light has found every crack in your keep.
Kneel now and call it sunstroke.
Check. The shade you seek does not exist.
Crowns glitter best right before they melt.
The sun stares down at your king. The sun does not blink.
Daybreak comes for you, and it is not gentle.
check_received: You dare cast a shadow on Sunspire?
A candle challenges the noon. Adorable.
The sun has weathered eclipses grander than you.
Dim me? Armies of night have tried.
My king stands in his own light. It does not flicker.
Insolence! Magnificent, doomed insolence.
Enjoy your moment of shade. Noon is coming back.
The horizon is full of those who challenged the dawn.
player_blunder: Staring into the sun, were you?
The light revealed your plan. There was no plan.
Glory blinds. So, it seems, does folly.
The sun saw that. The sun sees everything. Regrettably.
You have donated your kingdom to the day.
Even my shadow played better, and it only mimics.
A blaze of glory requires glory.
The dawn applauds. Mockingly.
player_undo: The sun does not rise twice for your convenience.
Unmove all you wish. Noon still comes.
You cannot pull back a shadow at dawn — yet you try.
Radiance never retraces. That is why it is radiant.
A take-back, in front of the sun itself. Bold shame.
Even eclipses commit. You should study them.
Daylight watched your first choice. It laughs at the second.
Wind back the board; the light has already judged.
endgame_win: The sun sets on you alone. I keep the sky.
Sunspire shines. The board is scorched clean.
A cloud passed. The sky does not recall its name.
Radiance, vindicated.
Look upon my noon and despair politely.
The light wins. This is not news.
Your shadow was the best of you, and it has fled.
The sun kneels for no one. You kneel for the sun.
endgame_lose: An eclipse. They are brief, and then the burning.
You have won the night. The dawn is already dressing for war.
The sun sets. Consult your histories on what follows.
Enjoy the dark. It suits you.
Pride dims. Pride does not die.
Savor dusk, my friend. I own the other end of it.
The horizon holds my banner. It will rise.
One night. You have purchased one night.

game_start: Honor rides the high wind. Try to keep sight of us.
Skyloft looks down on your position. Literally, and otherwise.
The falcon stoops only for worthy prey. Flatter yourself.
We fight clean, strike fast, and mourn briefly.
The high wind carries our banners and your doubts.
Look up. Keep looking up. That is where the war is.
Wings before crowns. Begin.
May your play deserve the height of my attention.
player_captured: The stoop was clean. Your {piece} never saw the sky darken.
Taken on the wing, with honor.
From this height, your {piece} was already small.
The talon closes once. It is enough.
A swift end is the only courtesy war allows.
It flew too low. Most things do.
The wind keeps what the falcon drops.
Struck fair, struck fast, struck first.
rival_captured: A feather lost in a clean fight. So be it.
You struck one of mine fairly. I will return the favor. Fairly.
The flock climbs higher when it grieves.
Honor concedes the strike. The sky concedes nothing.
That {piece} died on the wing. There are worse deaths.
Well struck. The sky files no complaint. I do.
Feathers fall. The bird does not.
You have earned an honorable enemy. Few are so lucky.
check_given: The shadow of wings crosses your throne.
Your king is in the open field, and I am in the sun.
Check, called fairly, from above.
The falcon has marked your king. Marks fade slowly.
Height, sight, strike. Your Grace, that is all war is.
The wind howls at your battlements now.
Look to your king. The sky already has.
No walls reach high enough. None ever have.
check_received: A bold cast. Honor acknowledges it. Altitude laughs at it.
You aim arrows at the wind.
My king perches high. Climb, if you dare the fall.
Threat noted, and answered from above.
The falcon dives through worse than courage.
You have reached for the sky. Now comes the reaching back.
Fair strike. The reply will also be fair. And faster.
Wings do not tremble. They tilt.
player_blunder: You flew into the cliff with your eyes open.
Even fledglings check the wind first.
An honorable fight was offered. You brought that instead.
From up here, we all saw it coming. All of us.
The wind gasped. The wind never gasps.
You have grounded yourself, saving me the stoop.
A wet hen glides better.
You fell without even the dignity of being pushed.
player_undo: A dive abandoned mid-air. The wind logs it as a fall.
Honor flies forward. What is this backward flapping?
Take the move back cleanly, at least. Form matters.
The falcon strikes once, true. It never asks the sky again.
From up here, a take-back looks like a stumble.
The high wind heard your nerve fail. It carries such news.
Retract and refly — the quarry is still faster than doubt.
A clean miss beats a smudged do-over. Noted on your honor.
endgame_win: The sky keeps its own. The field keeps you.
Checkmate, struck clean from the high wind.
Honor is satisfied. The falcon is fed. Good day.
Your banners lie flat. Ours never touched the ground.
You fought the vertical war and lost it.
Skyloft adds a crest to the aerie wall.
It ends where it began: with us above.
Salute your conqueror. The sun is behind me; squint.
endgame_lose: Well flown. The falcon salutes, and climbs to return.
You have won the ground. Keep it. We keep the sky.
Defeat, taken with honor. Returned in time, with talons.
The wind shifts. It always shifts back.
Clip one falcon and the whole aerie sharpens.
Honor in defeat is still honor. Remember I said so.
The high wind circles. So shall we.
You beat the bird, never the height.

game_start: The river binds us all. Today it binds you to me.
Rivergate is patient. The current is not.
We have outlasted every stone thrown at us. Throw yours.
Sit by the river long enough, and your king floats past.
The trout swims against the current for sport. This is sport.
Slow water wears down mountains. Imagine what it does to you.
Begin. The river has already begun.
Every game flows one way in the end. Ours.
player_captured: The current took your {piece}. The current was always going to.
Swept downstream, with the rest of your plans.
Patience, cast, catch. Your {piece} took the lure.
The river collects tolls at Rivergate. That was one.
Another stone worn smooth.
